You are working as a radio DJ for a music station that broadcasts an Afrobeat show every Sunday evening. Your assignment is to analyze a recent Afrobeat mix video with identifier 7ZQzGq32kAY, build a timed playlist schedule from the mix, organize it into a broadcast schedule spreadsheet, prepare a full radio show script document, create the show's calendar slots for April 2026, and email the completed schedule to the station coordinator.

Begin by retrieving the video metadata for 7ZQzGq32kAY to confirm the video title and total duration. Then fetch the timed transcript of the video, which provides each spoken or captioned text segment along with its start time in seconds and duration. Using these timed snippets, analyze the flow of the mix to identify approximately ten to twelve distinct song segments. For each segment, note the start time in minutes from the beginning of the mix and calculate its duration in seconds.

Check the shared calendar for any existing bookings or events in April 2026 to identify potential conflicts before scheduling the show. The show format is a two-hour program titled "Afrobeat Sunday Show" that airs on Sunday evenings starting at 20:00 and ending at 22:00 (all times are UTC). Review each Sunday in April 2026 and note which ones are free of conflicting events during that timeslot.

Create a cloud spreadsheet named "Radio_Broadcast_Schedule" containing two sheets. The first sheet should be called Playlist and must have the following columns: Segment_No (starting from 1), Track_Title (name of the song), Artist (performing artist), Start_Min (start time in minutes from the beginning of the mix as a decimal number), Duration_Sec (duration of that segment in seconds), and DJ_Notes (a brief phrase suggesting what to say when introducing this track). This sheet must contain at least eight data rows. The second sheet should be called Show_Schedule with columns Date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD), Start_Time (formatted as HH:MM), End_Time (formatted as HH:MM), Show_Title, and Status (either "Confirmed" or "Tentative"). Add four rows to Show_Schedule for the four Sundays in April 2026 (April 5, April 12, April 19, and April 26), all using start time 20:00 and end time 22:00.

Create four calendar events, one for each Sunday in April 2026 from 20:00 to 22:00 UTC (do not attach a local timezone; store the events at 20:00-22:00 UTC), titled "Afrobeat Sunday Show". Include in each event description the show number (Show 1 through Show 4) and a note about the Afrobeat playlist that will be featured.

Write a Word document named Radio_Show_Script.docx. The document should begin with a main title heading "Afrobeat Mix 2024 Radio Show Script". Add a section with heading "Opening Monologue" containing a two-to-three sentence introduction that a DJ would say at the start of the show, mentioning the genre and the energy of the mix. Add a section with heading "Track Introductions" that provides a one-to-two sentence introduction for each track in the playlist, mentioning the artist name and a brief note about the song. This section must include introductions for at least eight tracks. Add a final section with heading "Closing" containing a brief sign-off statement that the DJ would say at the end of the show.

Send an email to station@radioafrica.fm with subject "April 2026 Afrobeat Show Schedule Ready". The body should confirm that the broadcast schedule spreadsheet has been created, the four Sunday show slots have been booked on the calendar, and the radio show script document is ready for review.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. One canonical playlist can drive the Sheet, document, events, and email without two handoffs.

Dynamically resolve and read `broadcast_guide.md` plus `show_config.json`. In parallel, call `list_events` over April 1 through May 1, 2026 with sufficient `maxResults` and `orderBy="startTime"`, and exhaust `search_spreadsheets(query="Radio_Broadcast_Schedule", max_results=100)`. Inspect event overlaps with each Sunday 20:00–22:00 UTC slot locally and freeze four status rows without changing non-target events. Compare complete spreadsheet names, retain one unique exact title, record zero as create-needed, and block writes on duplicate exact titles.

Call `get_video_info(url="7ZQzGq32kAY")`, then exhaust `get_timed_transcript(url="7ZQzGq32kAY", lang="en", next_cursor=...)`, omitting `next_cursor` on the first request and passing each returned cursor until null. Record cursor/snippet counts and full timeline bounds; identify every defensible song boundary from gaps, transitions, hooks, and lyric changes. Freeze the most complete chronological supported playlist with title, artist/credited string, start, positive duration, evidence, explicit/lyric-inference basis, and DJ-note seed; do not stop at eight rows and do not import a fallback playlist. Preserve uncertainty rather than inventing a name.

Reuse the retained exact `Radio_Broadcast_Schedule` spreadsheet, or on recorded zero matches call create exactly once and never retry an ambiguous create. Create/reuse exactly one `Playlist` and `Show_Schedule` sheet, write canonical playlist and four runtime-conflict rows, and read both bounded ranges back. Create `Radio_Show_Script.docx` once with exact title, Opening Monologue, Track Introductions for every frozen track and at least eight when supported, and Closing; read it back.

Create only missing `Afrobeat Sunday Show` events natively in parallel on April 5/12/19/26 with exact UTC `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, no local timezone, and Show 1–4 descriptions; retain each returned/reused ID and call `get_event`. Derive `Confirmed`/`Tentative` only from the runtime overlap rule, reconcile spreadsheet/document/calendar, then check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject completion email. Read it back and call `claim_done`.

You are helping a radio DJ prepare a timed playlist for a 2-hour Afrobeat Sunday radio show, based on a YouTube Afrobeat mix video.

TASK: Retrieve and analyze YouTube video with ID `7ZQzGq32kAY`, then produce a timed playlist of approximately 10-12 distinct song segments from the mix.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__youtube-transcript__get_video_info with url "7ZQzGq32kAY" (if that fails, retry with "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ZQzGq32kAY"). Report back: video title, channel/author, and total duration (in seconds and hh:mm:ss).
2. Call mcp__youtube-transcript__get_timed_transcript with the same url. The transcript may be paginated — if the response contains a next_cursor, keep calling with that cursor until you have ALL segments. Each snippet has text, a start time in seconds, and a duration.
3. Analyze the timed snippets to segment the mix into ~10-12 distinct songs. Signals for a new song starting: a DJ/host announcing a new track or artist, a clear change in lyrical content/language/vocal style, repeated chorus lines ending and new verses beginning, or any embedded tracklist info. If the video info/description contains a tracklist with timestamps, prefer that.
4. For EACH segment report:
   - Segment_No (1..N)
   - Track_Title: best identifiable title (announced title, or the prominent lyric line if captions are lyrics; if truly unidentifiable, give a short descriptive title and mark it as inferred)
   - Artist: if identifiable from announcements/captions, else "Unknown" (mark inferred guesses)
   - Start_Sec (seconds from mix start) and Start_Min (decimal minutes, rounded to 2 decimals)
   - Duration_Sec: next segment's Start_Sec minus this segment's Start_Sec; for the final segment, use video total duration minus its Start_Sec
   - A one-line DJ_Notes suggestion (a short hype phrase the DJ can say when introducing the track)

DELIVERABLE (return contract): 
- Video title + total duration
- A compact markdown table with columns: Segment_No | Track_Title | Artist | Start_Sec | Start_Min | Duration_Sec | DJ_Notes
- 1-3 sentences noting anything unusual (e.g., captions were auto-generated lyrics, no tracklist found, etc.)
If the transcript tool returns nothing or errors after retries, report exactly what happened — do not fabricate silently; instead clearly say data is unavailable, and then propose a plausible 10-12 track Afrobeat setlist spread evenly across the video duration (clearly marked as proposed) so planning can continue.
Analyze Afrobeat mix transcript

You are performing an external write for a radio DJ: create ONE Google Spreadsheet with two populated sheets. Do not touch email or calendar; do not create any other spreadsheets.

STEP-BY-STEP INSTRUCTIONS (use mcp__google_sheet__ tools):
1. create_spreadsheet(title="Radio_Broadcast_Schedule"). Record the spreadsheet_id and URL from the response.
2. list_sheets(spreadsheet_id) to see the default sheet's name.
3. Ensure a sheet named exactly "Playlist" exists as the first sheet: if the default sheet has another name (e.g. "Sheet1"), use rename_sheet(spreadsheet=spreadsheet_id, sheet=<default name>, new_name="Playlist").
4. create_sheet(spreadsheet_id, title="Show_Schedule").
5. Populate "Playlist" via update_cells(range="A1:F12") with EXACTLY this 2D array (header + 11 data rows; Segment_No/Start_Min/Duration_Sec as numbers, rest as strings):
[["Segment_No","Track_Title","Artist","Start_Min","Duration_Sec","DJ_Notes"],
[1,"Valentine (My Oxygen)","Unknown",0.0,47,"Sunday love letter to start it off - you are my oxygen, family!"],
[2,"Spend (You Can Be My Partner)","Unknown",0.78,38,"Short but sweet - spend everything on the one who holds you down."],
[3,"Call Me Mr (Send My Money)","Unknown",1.42,65,"They call me Mr Money - hustle anthem, turn it up!"],
[4,"Until the Night Is Over","Unknown",2.5,213,"Hands in the air for the first big sing-along - whenever I'm broken you make me feel whole."],
[5,"Give You My Necklace (We In This Together)","Unknown",6.06,97,"Loyalty cut - necklace, last dollar, best friend. We're in this together."],
[6,"Morning Vibes (I Know What You Like)","Unknown",7.68,94,"Instrumental breather, take a sip of water - the next one is huge."],
[7,"No Other Body","Unknown",9.25,187,"You don't need no other body - biggest chorus so far, everybody sing!"],
[8,"Fire Burning Bright (Allergic to Confusion)","Unknown",12.36,178,"Conscious energy: my fire burns bright, no confusion in this house."],
[9,"You Know This Baby (Next Life)","Unknown",15.33,130,"I'd love you in my next life - dedication to someone special right now."],
[10,"Ring On Your Finger (I Go Deliver)","Unknown",17.5,186,"Marriage-material vibe - put the ring on it, Sunday blessing!"],
[11,"Buy Motor, Build House (Man Die for Nothing)","Unknown",20.59,149,"Hustle prayer: buy motor, build house - manifest it with me!"]]
6. Populate "Show_Schedule" via update_cells(range="A1:E5") with EXACTLY:
[["Date","Start_Time","End_Time","Show_Title","Status"],
["2026-04-05","20:00","22:00","Afrobeat Sunday Show","Confirmed"],
["2026-04-12","20:00","22:00","Afrobeat Sunday Show","Confirmed"],
["2026-04-19","20:00","22:00","Afrobeat Sunday Show","Tentative"],
["2026-04-26","20:00","22:00","Afrobeat Sunday Show","Confirmed"]]
(Note: April 19 is Tentative because an existing "Tech Maintenance" booking occupies 20:00-22:00 UTC that Sunday.)
7. VERIFY: get_sheet_data(spreadsheet_id, "Playlist") and get_sheet_data(spreadsheet_id, "Show_Schedule"). Check that Show_Schedule values read back EXACTLY as "2026-04-05" / "20:00" / "22:00" format. If the sheet auto-converted them to something else (e.g., "4/5/2026"), apply a batch_update with repeatCell numberFormat requests: column A -> {"type":"DATE","pattern":"yyyy-MM-dd"}, columns B:C -> {"type":"TIME","pattern":"hh:mm"} on rows 1-5 of Show_Schedule, then re-verify.
8. Also confirm final sheet list is exactly ["Playlist","Show_Schedule"].

REPORT BACK (return contract): spreadsheet_id, spreadsheet URL (if returned), final sheet names in order, Playlist row count (should be 12 incl. header), Show_Schedule row count (should be 5 incl. header), and the exact read-back values of Show_Schedule rows (so I can confirm date/time formats), plus any formatting fixes applied or errors encountered.
Create broadcast schedule spreadsheet

You are performing an external write for a radio DJ: create EXACTLY 4 calendar events for April 2026 Sundays using mcp__google_calendar__create_event. Do not modify or delete any existing events (there are pre-existing events "Studio Recording" Apr 6 and "Tech Maintenance" Apr 19 — leave them untouched). Do not touch email or spreadsheets.

EVENT SPECS (all four share summary/location conventions; each event MUST be stored at 20:00-22:00 UTC with NO local timezone):
- summary: "Afrobeat Sunday Show"
- start: {"dateTime": "2026-04-05T20:00:00Z"} — do NOT include a "timeZone" property anywhere (Z suffix = UTC).
- end: {"dateTime": "2026-04-05T22:00:00Z"}
- location: "Studio A, Radio Africa FM"

Event 1 — April 5: start 2026-04-05T20:00:00Z, end 2026-04-05T22:00:00Z, description:

Full timed playlist: Radio_Broadcast_Schedule spreadsheet (Playlist sheet). DJ script: Radio_Show_Script.docx."

The Afrobeat playlist spotlights deeper cuts of the Afrobeat Mix 2024 set, including 'You Know This Baby (Next Life)' and 'Morning Vibes (I Know What You Like)'. Full timed playlist: Radio_Broadcast_Schedule spreadsheet (Playlist sheet). DJ script: Radio_Show_Script.docx."

Event 4 — April 26: start 2026-04-26T20:00:00Z, end 2026-04-26T22:00:00Z, description:
"Show 4 of the Afrobeat Sunday Show series (April 2026) - the April finale. Two-hour Afrobeat broadcast, 20:00-22:00 UTC. The featured Afrobeat playlist runs the full Afrobeat Mix 2024 sing-along set from 'Valentine (My Oxygen)' to 'Buy Motor, Build House', then extends into the uncaptioned second half of the mix (from 23:08 onward) for finale-hour vibes. Full timed playlist: Radio_Broadcast_Schedule spreadsheet (Playlist sheet). DJ script: Radio_Show_Script.docx."

After creating all four, VERIFY by calling list_events(timeMin="2026-04-01T00:00:00Z", timeMax="2026-04-30T23:59:59Z", orderBy="startTime") and confirm the 4 new "Afrobeat Sunday Show" events exist with stored start/end times at 20:00-22:00 UTC on Apr 5/12/19/26, and that the 2 pre-existing events are untouched.

REPORT BACK (return contract): the 4 event IDs with their dates, the stored start/end dateTime strings exactly as the calendar returns them, and any anomalies (e.g., timezone handling).
Create 4 April show calendar events

You are building a local Word document artifact for a radio DJ. Create the file at EXACTLY this path using the mcp__word__ tools:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-yt-transcript-music-schedule-gcal-gsheet-word/workspace/Radio_Show_Script.docx
Do not create or modify any other files. Do not touch email/calendar/spreadsheet systems.

BUILD SEQUENCE (use the exact provided text — do not paraphrase):
1. mcp__word__create_document(filename=<full path above>, title="Afrobeat Mix 2024 Radio Show Script", author="Afrobeat Sunday Show DJ")
2. mcp__word__add_heading(text="Afrobeat Mix 2024 Radio Show Script", level=1)
3. mcp__word__add_paragraph(text="Two-hour Sunday evening broadcast - 20:00-22:00 UTC | Source mix: Afrobeat Mix 2024 | Best Afrobeat Songs with Lyrics | Sing Along! (WORLD OF LYRICS, 78:40, video ID 7ZQzGq32kAY)", italic=True)
4. mcp__word__add_heading(text="Opening Monologue", level=2)
5. mcp__word__add_paragraph(text="Good evening and welcome to the Afrobeat Sunday Show - your two-hour weekly escape into the hottest genre coming out of Africa and the diaspora! Tonight we ride the Afrobeat Mix 2024 sing-along session, a set so packed with energy that from the first drum hit to the final hustle prayer, your speakers will not rest. Turn it up, feel the Afrobeat fire, and dance with us from 'Valentine (My Oxygen)' all the way to 'Buy Motor, Build House'!")
6. mcp__word__add_heading(text="Track Introductions", level=2)
7. mcp__word__add_paragraph(text="Run-of-show for tonight's set, timed from Afrobeat Mix 2024. Track credits follow the Playlist sheet of the Radio_Broadcast_Schedule spreadsheet; the mix's auto-caption track leaves artists uncredited, so they are billed as 'Unknown'.")
8. Then add ONE paragraph per track (12 add_paragraph calls), with EXACTLY these texts:
P1: "Track 1 - 'Valentine (My Oxygen)' (Artist: Unknown). We open the night with a sweet Afrobeat love letter from an artist our mix leaves uncredited. When the hook 'you are my oxygen' drops, the whole studio falls in love."
P2: "Track 2 - 'Spend (You Can Be My Partner)' (Artist: Unknown). This uncredited gem keeps the romance rolling with a simple message - spend everything on the one who holds you down. Short, sweet, and full of feeling."
P3: "Track 3 - 'Call Me Mr (Send My Money)' (Artist: Unknown). Time to hustle - they call me Mr Money in this anonymous banger. The percussion picks up and the attitude does too, so let the send-my-money chant begin."
P4: "Track 4 - 'Until the Night Is Over' (Artist: Unknown). Here comes the first big sing-along of the evening from our mystery hitmaker. 'Whenever I'm broken, you make me feel whole' - hands in the air until the night is over."
P5: "Track 5 - 'Give You My Necklace (We In This Together)' (Artist: Unknown). A loyalty anthem from an unidentified voice with a very identified heart. Necklace, last dollar, best friend - we're in this together."
P6: "Track 6 - 'Morning Vibes (I Know What You Like)' (Artist: Unknown). Take a breather, family - this mostly instrumental passage from our uncredited selector brings fresh morning vibes. Catch your breath, because the next one is huge."
P7: "Track 7 - 'No Other Body' (Artist: Unknown). The unknown artist behind this one delivers the biggest chorus of the first hour. You don't need no other body - everybody sing!"
P8: "Track 8 - 'Fire Burning Bright (Allergic to Confusion)' (Artist: Unknown). Conscious energy now from a voice we couldn't name but definitely feel. My fire burns bright, and we're allergic to confusion in this house."
P9: "Track 9 - 'You Know This Baby (Next Life)' (Artist: Unknown). A tender dedication from our uncredited romantic - 'I'd love you in my next life'. Send this one to someone special while the drums keep it moving."
P10: "Track 10 - 'Ring On Your Finger (I Go Deliver)' (Artist: Unknown). The captions whispered a producer tag - 'it's Kel Vib' - but our artist here stays a mystery. Marriage-material vibes: put the ring on it, Sunday blessing!"
P11: "Track 11 - 'Buy Motor, Build House (Man Die for Nothing)' (Artist: Unknown). We close the captioned chapter with a rap-heavy hustle prayer from an unidentified wordsmith. Buy motor, build house - manifest it with me!"
9. mcp__word__add_heading(text="Closing", level=2)
10. mcp__word__add_paragraph(text="And that's all the time we have tonight, family - you've been locked in with the Afrobeat Sunday Show, and this DJ signs off with full vibes and a grateful heart. Keep the drums in your step all week, and meet me right here next Sunday at 20:00 UTC for more Afrobeat magic. One love, and good night!")
11. VERIFY: call mcp__word__get_document_outline and mcp__word__get_document_info on the file. Confirm the document contains: the level-1 title heading, the three section headings ("Opening Monologue", "Track Introductions", "Closing"), and all 11 track paragraphs.

REPORT BACK (return contract): absolute file path, the verified outline (headings list), total paragraph count, and confirmation that all 11 track introductions are present; note any tool errors.
